topic.title: React vs Next.js: Library vs Full-Stack Framework

hook: React is a UI library. Next.js is a complete full-stack framework. Here is when to use each.

slides.headline: React vs Next.js: Understanding the Core Difference
slides.body: Every web developer encounters the choice: start with pure client-side React (Vite) or adopt full-stack Next.js. The right choice depends on your rendering and SEO needs.
slides.visualSuggestion: React atomic icon vs Next.js full-stack framework shield

slides.headline: Client Rendering vs Full-Stack Capabilities
slides.body: Pure React runs entirely in the client browser, relying on Single Page Application (SPA) routing and client-side data fetching. Next.js provides hybrid rendering: Server Components, Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Static Generation (SSG), and API routes out of the box.
slides.visualSuggestion: Client Browser Execution vs Node.js Server Runtime Rendering

slides.headline: SEO & Initial Page Load Performance
slides.body: Client React downloads an empty HTML shell and large JavaScript bundle before rendering content. Next.js streams pre-rendered HTML from the server, improving Time to First Byte (TTFB) and search engine discoverability.
slides.visualSuggestion: Empty HTML bundle wait vs Server Rendered Pre-built HTML Stream

slides.headline: Operational Complexity & Deployment
slides.body: A pure React SPA can be hosted on static edge CDNs (Cloudflare Pages, S3) for pennies with zero server maintenance. Next.js requires a Node.js server or specialized edge compute runtime (Vercel, AWS ECS) for dynamic SSR.
slides.visualSuggestion: Static CDN Edge bucket vs Dedicated Node Server Infrastructure

slides.headline: Decision Matrix: When to Pick Which
slides.body: Choose pure React (Vite) for authenticated dashboards, offline PWAs, or internal tools. Choose Next.js for content-heavy sites, public e-commerce, and platforms requiring aggressive SEO and fast first-load times.
